newsitem.title: USA: House clears way for Barshefsky as trade chief.
newsitem.headline: House clears way for Barshefsky as trade chief.

text.p: The House of Representatives Tuesday cleared the way for Charlene Barshefsky to take office as U.S. Trade Representative.
By voice vote the House cleared a measure waiving a legal barrier against President Bill Clinton's nominee and sent to to the president for signature.
The measure waived a law barring anyone who previously represented a foreign government in a trade dispute with the United States from occupying the trade post.
The waiver was needed because Barshefsky represented the Canadian lumber industry in a dispute with the United States while she was with a Washington law firm.
The Senate approved the legislation last week and also voted to confirm Barshefsky on 99-1 vote. The House approved the waiver on a voice vote with only a few members in the chamber.
